snippets.output: The patient's vital signs indicate hypovolemic shock, and he suggests potential chronic alcohol use.

Sparse hair and rash suggest possible nutrient deficiencies. Loose bowel movements can be a sign of malabsorption or another underlying condition affecting nutrient absorption. Poor wound healing indicates a possible deficiency in nutrients essential for tissue repair.

Riboflavin (Vitamin B2) deficiency can cause sore throat, redness and swelling of the lining of the mouth and throat, cracks or sores on the outsides of the lips (cheilitis), and at the corners of the mouth (angular stomatitis).

Thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency is commonly associated with chronic alcohol use. Symptoms include beriberi and Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, but it does not typically cause hair loss or poor wound healing.
Vitamin C deficiency, known as scurvy, presents with poor wound healing, perifollicular hemorrhages, gingival disease, and can also present with rash (especially around the mouth) and hair loss.
Vitamin D deficiency mainly affects bone health, causing rickets or osteomalacia, and is less associated with hair loss or wound healing directly.

Zinc deficiency symptoms include alopecia (hair loss), dermatitis (especially around body orifices), diarrhea, and impaired wound healing. The combination of alopecia, rash at the corners of the mouth, diarrhea, and poor wound healing is most consistent with Zinc deficiency. The most likely deficiency in this patient is Zinc.
